newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW-LME reforms to be completed this year.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-LME reforms to be completed this year.

text.p: Reforms to boost transparency on the London Metal Exchange (LME) will largely be in place by the end of this year, LME Chief Executive David King said on Monday.
"The vast majority (of the reforms) will be in place by the end of the year," he said in an interview with Reuters on the sidelines of an international copper conference in Kobe, western Japan.
"In some cases introducing the enhanced transparency requires technological enhancement. It may take longer rather than sooner to introduce some of the procedures," he said.
"We're working on just about every issue concurrently," he added. "Some will find their way to the table sooner than others."
Last week the LME began daily reporting of warehouse stock levels, compared with its prior practice of twice-weekly reporting.
King said the LME had not yet appointed two new board members following its decision last month to increase the size of its board to 18 from 16.
He added that the exchange was working closely with Britain's Securities and Investments Board (SIB), which last December issued a review of the LME in response to the Sumitomo Corp copper affair.
King added that he expected the reforms would enhance the LME's dominant position in the world's base-metal markets.
"We already have the lion's share of the market. We're enhancing our procedures, which should consolidate our dominance," he said.

LME reforms currently under review would include reporting the existence of large positions in the market or the concentration of a certain percentage of warehouse stocks in the hands of a single market participant, although the holders' identity would not be disclosed.
The LME is also looking at issues such as how to address conflicts of interest, King said.
He added that the exchange is increasing its executive staff to 50 from 40, mostly in the area of compliance.
King was in Kobe for a meeting of the International World Copper Council (IWCC).
